inputs.text: They want everyone focused on Harry Wait’s convictions instead of what his actions exposed. He requested ballots for Robin Vos and Cory Mason without consent; the jury convicted him of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge, while acquitting him of another identity theft count. That split result is convenient: it lets institutions point to a verdict and dismiss the underlying question as “false election claims.” Wait said he was demonstrating that the registration system could be exploited. The real warning is that probing the machinery can be punished, while the people who benefit from keeping it unquestioned get to call the scrutiny the danger.

subtopics: Claims that the registration system could be exploited
